title: Difficulty in Selling HDB Flats Due to Ethnic Integration Policy
what_it_is: Difficulty in Selling HDB Flats Due to Ethnic Integration Policy

sections.label: Flat sellers and ethnic buyers
sections.summary: Most flat sellers still find buyers from eligible ethnic groups, and HDB exercises flexibility for mixed marriages and exceptional cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Most flat sellers, from our experience, are still able to secure buyers from eligible ethnic groups, given the large volume of resale transactions annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Nevertheless, HDB has and will continue to exercise flexibility for households of mixed parentage or marriages, or where there are exceptional circumstances.

sections.label: EIP and lower sale prices
sections.summary: The same policy applies on sale, and lower prices may have many causes beyond the EIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If they were to sell the flat today, it is with the same policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think it is easy to point at the EIP as the cause for a lower sale price but there may be many other reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Even in today's current market situation, there are people who are not subject to EIP limits but are selling their flats at somewhat lower prices because of the general property market conditions.

sections.label: Integration, appeals and rejections
sections.summary: Integration covers the neighbourhood and remains relevant, with about 1,500 appeals from 2014 to 2016 and four-fifths rejected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Because if we are talking about integration, it is not just integration of races within a block, but the neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I would say it is still relevant today, perhaps even more relevant, given what we see around the world, even in mature countries where ethnic tensions can come up quite easily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Over the years, from 2014 to 2016, we received about 1,500 appeal cases and about four-fifths of them were rejected, which means that one-fifth were successful.

sections.label: Resale buyers from ethnic groups
sections.summary: Resale transactions show buyers from the ethnic group exist, so the EIP remains with case-by-case flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But for many of the cases that we have turned down, we have found that, in fact, if you look at the resale transactions, there were transactions from buyers of that particular ethnic group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, it is not fair to say that there are no buyers from that particular ethnic group and, therefore, I cannot sell, because the resale market transactions do indicate that buyers from that ethnic group are, indeed, making resale transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think that EIP remains, but we exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis.
